item.title: Amazon S3 Vectors now supports metadata pre-filtering for higher recall on filtered searches (5 minute read)
item.description: AWS has introduced metadata pre-filtering for Amazon S3 Vectors to improve recall on filtered queries. The feature evaluates metadata filters before running a similarity search and supports up to 100 filter constraints per query. On highly selective filters, pre-filtering returns up to five times more matching vectors than previous methods. It is available immediately at no additional cost and works on existing indexes without requiring data re-ingestion.

item.title: Cloudflare Containers, rebuilt to scale agent sandboxes (15 minute read)
item.description: Cloudflare has rearchitected its Containers service to handle agent workloads, allowing code to select the image and instance type at runtime. The update introduces a new scheduling policy that starts containers six times faster, with median startup times falling from over four seconds to 648 milliseconds in independent benchmarks. A filesystem snapshots feature is also available in public beta to let workspaces save and restore their state.

item.title: Building a post-quantum certificate authority with Merkle Tree Certificates (10 minute read)
item.description: Cloudflare is launching a certificate authority that will support Merkle Tree Certificates (MTCs), targeting early 2027 for inclusion in Chrome's Quantum-resistant Root Store. The company will provide standard MTC issuance at no cost. MTCs batch certificates into an append-only Merkle tree to address the scaling issues of post-quantum cryptography, which can increase log storage requirements by 40 times. Cloudflare successfully tested the technology with Chrome, serving billions of MTCs and finding that median performance was 9% faster than classical signature chains.

item.title: We tested our own WAF with frontier AI models. Here's what we found (9 minute read)
item.description: Cloudflare built a dynamic testing tool that uses large language models to iterate attack payloads against its Web Application Firewall. The system ran 1,107 attempts across six attack categories and recorded 49 findings that required human review. Cloudflare used these results to release new detections for SSRF attacks and improve an existing cloud metadata rule.

item.title: How to justify investment in a platform (7 minute read)
item.description: Gartner forecasts that 40% of companies will downgrade autonomous AI agents by 2027 due to governance gaps found after production incidents. Google's DORA 2025 research found that 90% of organizations already use an internal platform, and 76% have dedicated teams for them. Broadcom research shows 97% of IT leaders believe some public cloud spending is wasted, with cost now exceeding security as the primary concern.

item.title: DBX (GitHub Repo)
item.description: DBX is a 25 MB cross-platform database client that supports over 100 databases, including MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQLite, Redis, and MongoDB. It runs as a native desktop app on macOS, Windows, and Linux, or via Docker and web deployments, without requiring Java, Python, or bundled Chromium. The tool includes an AI assistant that generates SQL from natural language and an MCP server that lets coding agents query databases.

item.title: Hyperframes (GitHub Repo)
item.description: HyperFrames is an open-source framework that converts HTML, CSS, and seekable animations into deterministic MP4 videos. The toolkit ships 21 skills that teach AI coding agents the full production loop, from planning and writing valid HTML to rendering with FFmpeg. It renders video by seeking frames in headless Chrome to ensure the same input always produces the same output.

item.title: Cut AI agent cost and improve accuracy with Code Execution in the Datadog MCP Server (7 minute read)
item.description: Datadog's new Code Execution feature lets AI agents run sandboxed JavaScript against its MCP Server, querying, joining, and filtering data across multiple APIs before returning only relevant evidence to the model. Testing across four models showed accuracy gains up to 21.8 points alongside 73% fewer input tokens and 40% fewer tool calls.

item.title: The 4 levels of agentic software development (9 minute read)
item.description: Enterprise AI productivity gains depend on platform maturity rather than model choice, with four levels running from humans approving every change to fully autonomous agents. Most organizations sit between levels one and two, and shifting validation from a single human gate to a continuous loop marks the hardest, highest payoff transition.

item.title: Why Kubernetes RBAC Misconfigurations Are the Easiest Privilege Escalation You'll Ever Find (4 minute read)
item.description: Recurring Kubernetes RBAC mistakes, cluster-admin bound to service accounts, wildcard permissions, over-broad secrets access, and stale bindings that never expire, drive most cluster compromises rather than novel vulnerabilities.

item.title: Introducing cf: the agentic CLI for the entire Cloudflare API (7 minute read)
item.description: Cloudflare has introduced cf, a new command-line interface that allows agents to access over 3,000 operations across the entire Cloudflare API. Wrangler previously supported around 280 commands, and agent usage of that tool reached 48% last week. cf uses a unified API generation pipeline to standardize commands and defaults to JSON output for agents. Cloudflare will provide maintenance support for Wrangler for 18 months after the beta ends.

item.title: Self-driving infrastructure with Pulumi and Jev (5 minute read)
item.description: TypeSafe AI opened early access to Jev, a model that uses decision-making primitives to help apps manage infrastructure. Pulumi built GeoDeploy, an open-source tool that uses Jev to automatically compare prices and provision Kubernetes clusters across AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud.

item.title: Beyond Kubernetes at Modal: How to Scale 1 Million Concurrent Sandboxes in Seconds (5 minute read)
item.description: Modal engineers rebuilt their sandbox platform to support millions of concurrent sandboxes by replacing Kubernetes-style centralized coordination with distributed worker state and parallel scheduling. The redesign created one million sandboxes in under 60 seconds with sub-half-second startup times, prompting talk that infrastructure is splitting into separate coordination and execution planes.

item.title: How Uber Protects Against Retry Storms (12 minute read)
item.description: Uber added error ownership to its shared service-mesh infrastructure, so upstream services can distinguish failures they caused from errors merely propagated from deeper dependencies. During a major outage, the mechanism prevented an estimated 9.5 million unnecessary retry requests and reduced the maximum retry-storm radius across user-facing APIs from as high as 25 hops to 3.

item.title: BigQuery to ClickHouse at 15M Call Minutes a Day: What Broke, What We Fixed, and How We Cut Costs 6x (8 minute read)
item.description: Bolna migrated analytics from BigQuery to ClickHouse, moved expensive CDC deduplication into materialized views, and fixed missing TOASTed JSONB values with REPLICA IDENTITY FULL. Reducing intermediate application writes cut replication traffic, with Bolna reporting roughly 6× lower analytics costs and data availability improving from 5–15 minutes to 1–2 minutes after calls ended.

item.title: OpenShell (GitHub Repo)
item.description: OpenShell is an Apache-2.0 runtime for running autonomous agents inside isolated sandboxes with kernel-enforced filesystem, syscall, and network policies. Credentials are injected only for approved endpoints, while proposed policy changes are formally checked before they are applied. The platform also supports Kubernetes deployment, GPUs, and Python, TypeScript, Go, and Rust SDKs.

item.title: Pageindex (GitHub Repo)
item.description: PageIndex replaces vector indexes with a hierarchical tree index that allows LLMs to reason through documents like a human expert. The tool achieved 98.7% accuracy on FinanceBench, outperforming vector-based RAG.

item.title: Can your Postgres survive a bad query? (16 minute read)
item.description: Postgres memory limits such as work_mem apply per execution node and per worker rather than per query, allowing seemingly ordinary queries to consume many times the configured amount of memory. Recursive queries can be even more dangerous because some executor hash tables cannot spill to disk, creating workloads that can exhaust memory despite conservative configuration.

item.title: What Dependency Mocking Software Needs to Handle in a Cloud Native Architecture (4 minute read)
item.description: Traditional dependency mocking tools break down in cloud native architectures where services deploy independently and drift goes undetected. Effective tools need deployment event awareness, behavior captured from real traffic rather than specs, automatic handling of non-deterministic fields, and cross-service diff visibility, with eBPF-based traffic capture cited as one approach.

item.title: Scale your AI workloads faster and more efficiently with GKE Pod snapshots (4 minute read)
item.description: Google Kubernetes Engine adds Pod snapshots, capturing a workload's running CPU and GPU memory state to restore it on demand, cutting AI inference startup by up to 89 percent and loading a 70B parameter model in 37 seconds. Codeway's Retake cut startup to eight seconds using the feature.

item.title: Better prompt caching for GPT-6 (3 minute read)
item.description: OpenAI launched an improved prompt caching system for the GPT-6 family that delivers higher cache hit rates by default. Developers get discounts of up to 90% on cached input tokens when the system reuses shared prefixes within a 30-minute window. New tools include a Prompt Caching Dashboard to track hit rates and a diagnostics tool to investigate unexpected misses. Developers can also prewarm the cache to reduce latency or adjust reasoning effort between responses without breaking cache.

item.title: Cloudflare Introduces the Agent Development Stack Lifecycle to Replace Traditional SDLC (2 minute read)
item.description: Cloudflare introduced an Agent Development Lifecycle to replace traditional software pipelines with autonomous, event-driven systems for AI coding agents, built on its Workflows product and a new @cloudflare/ci tool. It adds OpenTelemetry-based observability and an Agent Access Model that issues short-lived, capability-limited credentials to prevent lateral movement.

item.title: Teaching a 9B model to investigate production alerts (9 minute read)
item.description: Datadog fine-tuned Qwen3.5-9B on traces from a larger teacher model to automate change attribution during incident investigations. The specialized student model achieved 87% of the teacher's recall while reducing inference costs by roughly 20 times to $0.003 per investigation. A single 40 GB A100 GPU can support approximately 100,000 of these investigations per week.

item.title: AI Now: Tech Workers Inquiry (6 minute read)
item.description: AI systems increasingly depend on hidden layers of human labor, including data labeling, content moderation, model evaluation, and other forms of contract work that shape how models behave. Making those labor relationships visible helps explain where AI systems get their capabilities, how failures are caught, and which costs are shifted onto workers outside the companies building the models.

item.title: Model Optimizer (GitHub Repo)
item.description: NVIDIA has open sourced its Model Optimizer library, which offers techniques like quantization, pruning, and distillation to accelerate deep learning models. The tool supports inputs from Hugging Face, PyTorch, or ONNX and exports optimized checkpoints for deployment frameworks like TensorRT-LLM and vLLM. Users can install the stable release via PyPI or use NVIDIA container images with the software pre-installed.

item.title: Harness-sdk (GitHub Repo)
item.description: Strands Agents is a new open-source SDK for building AI agents in Python and TypeScript. It offers a "harness" with benchmarked defaults for models and memory, or developers can use the underlying SDK to write their own agent loops. The toolkit includes support for tools, structured output, and model providers such as Amazon Bedrock, Anthropic, and OpenAI.

item.title: Docker Sandbox Kit Spec: Authority as Code (7 minute read)
item.description: The Docker Sandbox Kit Specification v3 defines how to package an agent's permissions and dependencies as an ordinary OCI image. The format specifies network rules, credentials, and volumes, allowing developer tooling to scan, sign, and diff agent authority changes. Docker Sandboxes is the first conforming runtime for the open source specification.

item.title: Global AI routing with <1% overhead on multi-cluster GKE Inference Gateway (6 minute read)
item.description: Google's multi-cluster GKE Inference Gateway pools globally distributed accelerator capacity behind a single endpoint, routing LLM traffic based on live KV-cache utilization rather than round-robin. A 17,000-node benchmark across three regions showed near-linear throughput scaling with less than 1 percent routing overhead and a 99.9 percent success rate.
